simple.meaning: חֲצֹצְרָה (chătsôtsᵉrâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a trumpet (from its sundered or quavering note).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 29 times across Numbers, 2 Kings, 1 Chronicles, 2 Chronicles, Ezra, and 3 more, beginning at Numbers 10:2. Its contexts include family line, offering, sacrifice, kingship, priesthood, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חֲצֹצְרָה (H2689).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: חֲצֹצְרָה (chătsôtsᵉrâh) / H2689 is traced through Numbers 10:2, Numbers 10:8, Numbers 10:9, Numbers 10:10 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.short: a trumpet (from its sundered or quavering note)
definitions.full: H2689. chatsotsrah חֲצֹצְרָה noun feminine clarion (Late Hebrew חֲצוֺצֶרֶת , Aramaic חֲצוֺצַרְתָּצ ) — mostly P and late; — absolute ׳ח Hosea 5:8 ; plural absolute חֲצֹצְרוֺת Num 10:8 22 t.; חֲצֹצְרֹת 10:9-10 , construct id. 31:6 ; 2Chr 13:12 ; חֲצוֺצְרֹת Num 10:2 ; clarion: 1 as secular instr . Hosea 5:8 (|| שׁוֺפָר ) 2Kin 11:14 (twice in verse) = 2Chr 23:13 (twice in verse). 2 as sacred instr . 2Kin 12:14 , especially for use by priests (only P, Psalm 98 and Chronicles). a. בח ׳תקע (of blowing a single long blast) Num 10:3-4 , 7 , 8 , to gather congregation or ׳נשׂיא together, and, on festivals, over sacrifice, 'to be remembered before ׳י ,' 10:10 . b. בח תרועה ׳תקע , or בח ׳הריע (of sounding alarm, — a series of quick blasts) for camps to move Num 10:5-6 , also in battle, 10:9 , 'to be remembered before ׳י ;' so 31:6 ; 2Chr 13:12 (compare 13:14 ), both ׳ח התרועה . c. especially in Chr's descriptions of ceremonies at festivals, to express rejoicing: 1Chr 13:8 ; 15:28 (|| שׁוֺפָר קוֺל ), 16:6 , 42 ; 2Chr 15:14 (|| שׁוֺפָר ), 20:28 ; 29:26-27 , Ezra 3:10 ; Neh 12:35 , 41 ; Psa 98:6 (|| שׁוֺפָר קוֺל ); בח קוֺל ׳הָרִים 2Chr 5:13 ; בח ׳מחצצרים 1Chr 15:24 ; 2Chr 5:12-13 , 13:14 ; in 29:28 this participle agrees with noun in sense , and is masculine; and the clarions (= players on the clarions) sounded . — The חֲצֹצְרָה , or (sacred) clarion, was a long, straight, slender metal tube, with flaring end, see Benz Archäol. 277 ; distinguished thus from the שׁוֺפָר which was originally a ram's horn, and probably always retained the horn-shape; the שׁוֺפָר is mentioned constantly in the earlier literature, and was used by watchmen, warriors, etc., as well as priests (see Benz ib. 276 and שׁוֺפָר ).
